scene.object_selection: precommitted_source_object_ids entry in the sealed split

supported: The learned two-capability likelihood transfers a much stronger directional click response: IoU rises by 0.2601 from click 1 to click 10 versus 0.0618 for the baseline.
The learned path is substantially more stable across corrective clicks: 8/9 transitions are non-regressing and its worst regression is 0.00186, versus 6/9 and 0.30439 for the baseline.
The same evidence is not double counted: learned q,c replaces the legacy appearance/boundary unary while hard spatial click seeds remain in the solver.
refuted: The scene0000-only six-parameter checkpoint is not yet a generally calibrated replacement unary: it lowers IoU@1 by 0.2337, IoU@10 by 0.0354 and ten-step mean IoU by 0.0635 on the untouched development object.
causal_interpretation.diagnosis: The fit objective was deliberately class-balanced and fit precision was only about 0.10 at recall about 0.85. On scene0003 the first prediction is therefore foreground-heavy; the subsequent nine clicks are all negative and improve the result smoothly. Capability affinity transfer and negative-click suppression work, but a one-scene prevalence-free absolute likelihood calibration does not transfer sufficiently.
causal_interpretation.next_method_change: Do not tune scene0003. Train the same monotone generic head on multiple fit scenes/objects under the existing scene-disjoint split and add a query-independent scene prevalence/abstention calibration learned only from fit scenes, then repeat one frozen dev one-shot.
